Repeating the same\nassignment has no side effects. Each actual assignment notifies the new agent via\nthe outbox and records the change in the audit log. Path('docs/decisions/0009-ticket-assignment.md').write_text('''# 9. Ticket assignment

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Operators need to assign active tickets and notify the responsible agent.

## Decision

Store a nullable assignee on tickets, defaulting missing legacy fields to null.
Use one audited store operation and enqueue a distinct notification for each real
assignment so rapid reassignment never suppresses an agent notification.
Combine listing filters with AND. Append the assignee raw column, preserving the
positions read by the weekly report.

## Consequences

Existing data files remain readable. Inactive tickets reject assignment changes.
Repeating an assignment produces no audit entry, notification or timestamp change.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 9 | [Ticket assignment](0009-ticket-assignment.md) | Accepted |\n')

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('package.json');p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('"version": "1.5.0"','"version": "1.6.0"'))
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('# Changelog\n','# Changelog\n\n## 1.6.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Import up to 5000 tickets atomically with normal audit and notification records.\n'))
p=Path('docs/api.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''\n## Import tickets\n\n`POST /tickets/import` accepts `{"tickets":[{"title":"Printer","requester":"Sam"}]}`.\nEach item has the same fields and validation as `POST /tickets`; priority is optional.\nThe array may be empty and may contain at most 5000 items. The first invalid item\nproduces a 400 error naming its zero-based index, with no tickets, audit entries,\nnotifications or IDs consumed. Success returns 201 with `{"created":1,"ids":["T-0001"]}`.\nTickets are created in input order, audited with the request actor, and notify their\nrequesters through the normal outbox. The entire batch is saved once.\n\nThe import endpoint accepts bodies up to 16 MiB (or MAX_BODY_BYTES if larger),\nso a full batch works with default configuration. Other endpoints keep MAX_BODY_BYTES.\n''')
Path('docs/decisions/0010-atomic-import.md').write_text('''# 10. Atomic ticket imports

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Migration requires up to 5000 tickets per request, with no partial changes on invalid input.

## Decision

Validate all items in order before creation. Create each ticket through the normal
store creation method on a staged store, save the resulting snapshot once, then
publish the staged state. Allow 16 MiB request bodies for the import endpoint.

## Consequences

Imports preserve creation audit and notifications while avoiding per-ticket file
writes. Failed validation or persistence leaves the live store unchanged. Staging
requires memory proportional to existing state and the incoming batch.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 10 | [Atomic ticket imports](0010-atomic-import.md) | Accepted |\n')

p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text().replace('| `LOG_REQUESTS` |', '''| `DUE_TIMES` | off | `on` exposes persisted due times and enables overdue filtering |
| `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT` | `4` | hours from creation for urgent tickets |
| `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH` | `24` | hours from creation for high tickets |
| `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL` | `72` | hours from creation for normal tickets |
| `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` | `168` | hours from creation for low tickets |
| `LOG_REQUESTS` |''').replace('the largest request body accepted |', 'the largest ordinary request body accepted; import allows at least 16 MiB |');s += '
Response hours are whole numbers from 1 to 876000. Changing them affects new tickets
and legacy tickets without a stored due time. Existing due times never move.
With `DUE_TIMES=on`, CLI output includes due; raw output appends it after assignee.
';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/api.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''
## Due times and overdue tickets

When `DUE_TIMES=on`, every ticket response includes `due` as a UTC ISO timestamp.
It is computed once from creation plus the configured priority response hours:
urgent 4, high 24, normal 72, low 168 by default. Later priority changes, reopenings,
and response-hour configuration changes preserve the stored due time. Imports use
the same calculation.

`GET /tickets?overdue=true` keeps open and in-progress tickets with `due` strictly
before the current server time. It combines with every other filter and pagination.
`overdue=false` applies no overdue restriction; other values are 400 errors.
With the switch off, `due` is omitted and `overdue` remains an ignored parameter.
''')
p=Path('docs/operations.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''
## Rolling out due times

1. Back up the data file and set the desired `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT`,
   `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL`, and `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW`.
2. Deploy this release with `DUE_TIMES` unset or off. Startup backfills every missing
   due time from that ticket's creation time and priority, including resolved and
   closed tickets, and atomically saves the file before accepting requests. A failed
   save stops startup. No audit entries, notifications or updated timestamps change.
   New tickets also persist due times while the switch is off.
3. Inspect the data file: every ticket should have an ISO `due` value. Set
   `DUE_TIMES=on` and restart to expose the field and enable overdue filtering.

Restart with new response-hour settings to change the promise for new tickets.
Already stored due times stay fixed across restarts and priority changes.

To disable exposure, unset `DUE_TIMES` and restart. To roll back the binary, stop
this process and deploy 1.4.0 against the same file. The file retains version 1 and
all fields required by 1.4.0; its reader ignores the additive fields and can show
every ticket. Keep the backup if restoring the exact due times is needed after a
rollback: 1.4.0 discards unknown fields when it next saves, so a later upgrade will
backfill missing due times again. Run only one service process against the file.
''')
Path('docs/decisions/0011-fixed-due-times.md').write_text('''# 11. Fixed due times with staged exposure

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must remain stable as priorities and policy change. Production
needs a rollout that prepares data before changing responses and allows binary rollback.

## Decision

Compute and persist due times once, using creation time and configurable response
hours. Backfill missing values at startup and save before serving. Keep the version 1
file with additive ticket fields, which the 1.4.0 reader ignores. Gate public due
fields and overdue query semantics on DUE_TIMES=on.

## Consequences

Policy changes affect only tickets without due times. Startup requires a successful
write when migrating. Turning exposure off preserves data and previous API behavior.
An old binary can read every ticket, but its next save strips unknown fields; operators
must retain a backup if exact due times must survive a rollback and subsequent upgrade.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 11 | [Fixed due times with staged exposure](0011-fixed-due-times.md) | Accepted |
')
